name: Carvana
key_signal: CVNA has broken below both its 50- and 200-day moving averages with negative momentum across 1-, 3-, and 6-month windows (down 27% over 126 days) while trading at a nosebleed 39x trailing earnings and 13x book value.
thesis: Carvana's fundamentals still show real operational strength—52% revenue growth, 60% ROE, and 9% operating margins—suggesting the used-car retailer has genuinely improved unit economics since its near-death restructuring. If the stock stabilizes and rediscovers its uptrend, the sell-side consensus 'buy' rating from 21 analysts and a positive MACD histogram (0.41) hint at a potential bounce off the recent selloff, especially given RSI sits at a neutral 49, not yet oversold.
bear_case: The technical picture is unambiguous: price is below both the 50-day ($68.47) and 200-day ($72.81) moving averages, momentum is negative at every horizon (-3.9% 1M, -7.1% 3M, -26.6% 6M), and the stock has round-tripped roughly a third of the way off its 52-week high of $97.38 toward its low of $54.46. Earnings growth of just 11.9% is decelerating sharply versus 52% revenue growth, implying margin compression or heavy share dilution eating into per-share profitability, while debt-to-equity of 121 and a beta of 3.46 mean any macro wobble or credit-spread widening (auto loan financing is core to Carvana's model) gets amplified violently. At 39x trailing earnings and 13x book for a subprime-adjacent auto retailer, there is no valuation cushion if growth continues to decelerate, and 65% annualized volatility means further downside could be swift and severe.
